newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 1.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

A record 23,000 Australian households watched the Tyson-Holyfield fight live on pay-TV operator Foxtel. The event was offered in pay-per-view format, attracting 11 per cent of Foxtel's subscribers, and generated almost $1 million in revenue. Page 22

Australian Greg Norman clinched a stunning one-shot victory with a 20-foot putt on the 18th hole to take the St Jude Classic and his 17th title on the US PGA tour. The Shark's performance prompted former world No.1 Nick Price to call Norman "the greatest golfer in 20 years". Page 21

Australian Rugby League player Mark Geyer yesterday pleaded guilty to a grade-three reckless high tackle charge from Adelaide's Cameron Blair, accepting a media ban on himself. The charge carries a four-match penalty. Page 20
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian Rugby League has cleared Parramata prop Dean Pay of a charge for placing a player in a dangerous position, following expert testimony by Parramata coach Brian Smith. Pay is now cleared to play for the Australia team against the Rest of the World. Page 49

Cricket relations between Australia and Sri Lanka are on the mend, with PILCOM, the cricket World Cup body, set to pay Australia the $100,000 withheld after the boycott of the Colombo World Cup matches last year. Sri Lanka's fast bowler Chaminda Vaas is also in Sydney for treatment to his injured back at Concord Hospital. Page 48

The Australian Rugby Union has informed officials in the New South Wales, Queensland and the Australian Capital Territory that clearance from the national body is required before players can join overseas clubs during the domestic season. Page 49
THE AGE

The Australian Football League Tribunal last night issued one-match suspensions to Western Bull Dogs' Steve Kolyniuk, Melbourne's Marcus Seecamp and West Coast's Fraser Gehrig. Gehrig will sit out an important game with Adelaide on Friday, while Kolyniukwill miss a vital match against Carlton. Page B8

The Bombers have sealed a three-year contact with Essendon star James Hird that is worth more than $1.1 million. Hird, the 1996 Brownlow Medallist, wanted $500,000, but settled for about $375,000 to aid in bringing a positive aspect to the club which has suffered a series of losses and the sudden departure of football manager Danny Corcoran. Page B8

The Australian Football League is waiting for requested footage from Channel Seven television station to decide whether a notice of possible investigation from field umpire Grant Vernon into a clash between Carlton's Stephen Silvagni and West Coast's Ilija Grgic should be further explored. Page B8
THE HERALD SUN

Trainer Colin Anderson has asked the Bairnsdale Racing Club for compensation following a June 15 meeting in which the club allegedly declared the track dead before stewards downgraded the rating to slow after the first race. Page 65

Three bids for the construction of the Victoria Stadium have been received by the Docklands Authority. The project is expected to cost between $200 and $300 million, and the Australian Football League would need to schedule around 40 games a season to make it viable. Page 70

West Australian Jane Leary managed sixth place in the $245,500 Irish women's Open in Dublin yesterday. Leary's pro career-best performance saw her finish six strokes behind winner Patricia Meunier Lebouc at the Luttrellstown Castle course. Page 64
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian athletes Greg Bennet and Michellie Jones have won the third round of the ITU World Cup triathlon in Monte Carlo. Jones is the only Australian woman to win two world triathlon titles, while Bennet has so far gained two international victories in his career. Page 70

According to a high-ranking Soccer Australia official, former England manager and Australian Socceroo coach Terry Venables has been selected by the organisation to represent Australia on the English Football Association. Page 62
Australian skiff sailors Chris Nicholson and Daniel Phillips have grabbed a stunning win in the pair's first international regatta in the new 49ner class at the Kiel Week regatta in Germany. Page 67
